title: Button Property Editor (ver. 2025.0)
content:
Adjust button properties in the Property Editor. ## ## **Button Style Property Editor** ### Objective Use these options to edit button styles, materials for buttons/threads, and polygon optimization. #### **** ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Object Browser ▶ Property Editor Button **Side Panel** Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown menu ▶ Property Editor ### Operation Object Browser ▶ Select a button item in the Buttonhole Tab. → The properties are displayed in the Property Editor. Properties | Description ---|--- Information | Name | Enter a name for the Button. Shape | Select the type of button from the drop-down icon. Click the plus icon to [register the Button or Thread as an OBJ file](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358452715161). Click the CONNECT icon to open the CONNECT Store and download buttons. Thread Type | Select the thread type from Cross / Parallel / Square. Specification | Width (mm) | Decide the width of the button in millimeters. Link to Fastened Buttonhole | Toggle ON/OFF to enable or disable buttonhole fastening. Thickness (mm) | Decide the thickness of the button in millimeters. Weight (g) | Decide the thickness of the button in grams. Material Button / Thread | Type | Set the appropriate Button / Thread Type. Base Color | Color | Select the color of the base color. Base Color Map | Base Color Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from the Library/Folder. Recolor | Adjust the Transformation (Unified) by defining the Angle, Repeat U/V, and Position U/V. Desaturate | Desaturate the entire Base Color Map to remove color and convert it into grayscale or black and white. Switch | Color Switch: Easily and quickly switch the color of the texture to a new one without losing the accuracy of the chosen color. ![Switch Color.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438329467289) ※Note: For consistent results, the Base Color Map should contain 1 color. If the Base Color Map contains multiple colors, users may experience unexpected results. Normal Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder, generated with the generate icon. A base color map needs to be applied before this will work. Intensity | Adjust the intensity of the Normal map from -100 to 100. Displacement Map | Click the explore button and apply a texture image from Library/Folder, generated with the generate icon. A base color map needs to be applied before this will work. Amount | Adjust the maximum height of the displacement map. The white area of the displacement map shows the maximum height. Shift | Adjust the distance between the displacement map and the garment surface Clipping | Adjust to delete all geometries below the Clipping value. Particle Distance | Adjust the Particle Distance of newly created meshes. Keep Continuity | Extend the adjacent face to eliminate the boundary line. ※ Note: Only applicable to Welded OBJs. Transformation (Unified) | Apply transformation settings for Angle, Repeat U/V, and Position U/V.

``` | Opacity | Adjust the opacity level from 0 to 100. Opacity Map | RGB Mode | The encoded map with the alpha value in the RGB channel. Alpha Mode | The encoded map with the alpha value in the alpha channel. Reflection | Roughness | Intensity | Edit fabric gloss by adjusting the Intensity of the Roughness Map | Edit fabric gloss by adding and modifying the Roughness Map. Map | Select the Browse button next to the Map option to add a Roughness Map to the selected Fabric style. Map Intensity | Adjust the Map's Intensity. The range of Roughness map intensity was enlarged in (ver. 2024.2) Invert | Select to invert the gloss of the fabric. When this option is selected, the shiny part becomes dull and vice versa. To use the Specular Maps provided below version 6, check this option. Reflection Intensity | The greater/lesser the Reflection Intensity value is, the more reflective/dull the material or fabric is. Metalness | Adjust the metallic level. Higher value makes the surface more metallic. Metalness Map | Partially express metallics using a grayscale image. The white parts of the map appear metallic. Polygon Optimization | Count | Set the number of polygons. Plane | This is applied in the form of a texture when the Plane is activated. Count cannot be set on Plane activation. ![89308cd0-c743-465a-a7e8-153683d5631c](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438329672857) ## **Button Property Editor** ### Objective Use these options to edit button styles, including rotation, thread length, style of the button, and collision settings. #### **** ### Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Button ▶ Select/Move Button 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move Button ### Operation Selecting a button with the Select/Move or Select/Move Button tool displays its properties in the Property Editor. Property | Description ---|--- Angle | Enter the desired value for the rotation angle of buttons. Thread Length (mm) | Enter the desired value for thread length in millimeters (mm). Style | Select a button style. Collision | Set ON/OFF for the collision option. → Set it OFF to fix its location to avoid collision between the buttons and the Patterns. 2D Measurements | View the position of buttons in 2D Pattern with its size measurement. Reset | Resets the properties of the Button style to the Default Button properties.

title: USD file Compatibility (ver. 12.1)
content: ## Feature Overview With USD, a graphics standard file format, you can increase collaboration productivity with a variety of 3D software You can export clothing, avatars, and accessories with meshes and materials from Marvelous Designer as USD files. You can also import USD files created in other 3D software packages into Marvelous Designer. ## Import USD You can import an USD file as an avatar, a trim, or a scene/prop type. Cloth and avatar animations can also be exported/imported. (ver. 2024.1) ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below. **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import ▶ USD Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import (Add)▶ USD USD Layer Window ▶ Import Drag & drop an USD file on to the software **Setting - Import USD Dialog** Load Type | Open | All existing objects will be removed, leaving the imported file only. ---|---|--- Add | Add an object, keeping the existing objects. Object Type | Avatar | Import an USD file as an Avatar type. \- Objects imported as an Avatar type can be muti-selected. Trim | Import an USD file as a Trim type. \- The object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Trim type cannot collide with clothing. \- Set the collide option for a Trim type on the Property Editor by toggling on the Collision check-box. \- Select an trim object and toggle on the Glue icon on the gizmo to attach the object to clothing. \- Toggle on the Scale icon on the gizmo to scale the size of an object. Scenes & Props | When importing an object as Scenes & Props, the object will pass through the clothing while Simulation is on, as the Scenes & Props type do not have Collision. Auto Create Fitting Suit | A Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. Scale | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver.2024.1) | X, Y(Up), Z | Using Axis Conversion, you can change the orientation of the imported mesh. Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. Invert | Invert the selected axis. Translation | Align Bottom to Ground | When an object is placed below the ground, toggle on Align Bottom to Ground check-box to place the object imported above ground. ※ Note (ver. 2024.1): * It is recommended that the Animation Layer name not be changed. * When importing an Avatar that is a USD file format, [Motion files (.MTN)](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358363172249) cannot be applied to that avatar because it is not the default skeletal avatar type supported by Marvelous Designer. * If multiple skeletal animations (SkelAnimation) are loaded into the animation window, the upper most animation is played in the 3D Space. ### End Result The USD file is successfully imported into the software you set. A list of layers for the imported file can be found on the USD Layer window. \- If USD Layer window is not visible in the workspace, it will appear in a new window as a pop-up. ## Export USD You can export clothing, avatars or trims as an USD file. Cloth and avatar animations can also be exported. (ver. 2024.1) ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below: **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Export ▶ USD **Setting - Export USD Dialog** Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Select All Patterns | Either select or deselect all patterns. -Each pattern can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Select All Avatars | Either select or deselect all avatars/objects \- Each avatar/object can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Select All Graphics and Trims | Either select or deselect all graphics and trims \- Each graphic and trim can be individually selected from the drop-down menu. Single Object (ver. MD2024.0) | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects (ver. MD2024.0) | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Option (Ver. 2024.1) | Garment Animation (Ver. 2024.1) | Saves pattern cache animation. ※ Note : Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation (Ver. 2024.1) | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. ※ Note : Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache (ver. 2024.2) | Saves Avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver. 2024.2) | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. ### ※ Note (Ver. 2024.1): * It is recommended that the Animation Layer name not be changed. * To export a pattern and an avatar at the same time, select the avatar first and then select the patterns. ### End Result The USD file is successfully exported as you set. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. ## USD Layer Window A list of layers for the imported file can be found in the USD Layer window. ### Steps Follow the indicated guideline below: **Location** The drop-down list at the top center of all windows. ▶ USD Layer ![usd_layer_window.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438538423577) **1\. Buttons** Create | Create an USD file \- An USD file is created with the specified path and name, appearing in the USD Layer window. This file will be set as the Authoring Layer. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the directory where the USD is saved. ---|--- Import | Import an USD file Clear | Delete all the layers listed in the USD Layer. **2\. List of Layers** Authoring Layer | The default layer which is being used at the moment. \- When running Export to USD Layer for clothing, trims, scenes/props, they will be exported to the Authoring Layer. ---|--- Material | The default path where the Materials appear. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. Mesh | The default path where the Mesh appears. \- Users can name this path while running Export to USD Layer. **3\. Right Mouse Button****Menus - Layers** Click the right mouse button on the list of the layers to access the menus below. ![usd_layer_window2.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438532533785) Set Authoring Layer | Set the selected layer as active. \- The same can be done by double clicking the left mouse button** **This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is already set as the Authoring Layer. \- Where the selected layer is an USDZ (read only) \- Where the selected layer is missing. ---|--- Delete | Deleted the selected layer. This menu won't appear in the following situations: \- Where the selected layer is the Authoring Layer. Export USDZ from Layer | Export the selected layer as USDZ (read only) \- Once an USDZ is imported, it cannot be exported again. **4\. Export the Selected Object through Right Mouse Button Menus** To export your cloth and/or trim assets from Marvelous Designer as a USD file; select the assets from either 3D or 2D window, and click "Export to USD Layer" to export them to the Authoring Layer. This will update the USD file corresponding to the Authoring Layer. **Setting - Export to USD Layer** Prim | Mesh | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Mesh. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Mesh when exporting. ---|---|---|--- Material | Prim Path | Either select or deselect Material. \- You can name the Prim Path for the Material. \- When exporting the Material, a Texture folder is created within the folder where the USD is saved. All related textures will be saved in that Texture folder. Object | Single Object (ver. 2024.0) | Exports selected object as a single object. Multiple Objects (ver. 2024.0) | Exports selected object as multiple objects. Thin (ver. 2024.2) | Export USD without the rendering thickness. Thick (ver. 2024.2) | Export USD with the rendering thickness as Geometry. Unified UV Coordinates | Exports the texture data for all patterns to fit within UV coordinates Image Size | Set the size of the image in pixels Fill Texture Seams | Extend the scope of texture based on the texture's borders. Include Garment Simulation Data (ver. 2024.2) | USD export for garments, including the necessary data for simulation setup. Option (Ver. 2024.1) | Cache Animation (ver. 2024.1) | Saves pattern cache animation. ※ Note : Since Pattern Cache Animation is exported as a mesh itself, there is no separate Animation Type prim. Avatar Animation (ver. 2024.1) | Joint | Saves the animation data for Avatar animation as skeletal animation. ※ Note : Avatar Animation is exported to the USD Layer Window as a SkelAnimation type below SkelRoot. Cache (ver. 2024.2) | Saves avatar cache animation. Basic | Scale | Set the unit of scale. % | Adjust the scale in percentage. Axis Conversion (ver. 2024.2) | Up Axis | Select the up-axis used in the application where the file was imported from. Marvelous Designer will compare the up-axis of the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. ※ Note : In Marvelous Designer, the Y axis is the up-axis. * When exporting garment using Export to USD Layer, the exported output will differ depending on the 3D Garment Rendering Style state. If the 3D garment appears in Thick Textured Surface, it will be exported with thickness. ### End Result The USD file is successfully exported as you set it. * When saving the project file (*.zprj), the imported USD Layer and file information will be saved altogether. \- When opening this file, if the USD file path is missing, you can either create new or ignore it. Create new USD file path in replace of the missing one, using the right mouse button menus. * Please try out this **[USD sample file](https://s3.marvelousdesigner.com/newmdweb/helpcenter/manual/KoiFish_USD.zip) **we created with Marvelous Designer and see how the new USD support can benefit your workflow. Step by step tutorial for how to export this USD file from Marvelous Designer coming soon.
content_description: This web page provides a comprehensive guide on importing and exporting USD files in Marvelous Designer, enhancing collaboration and productivity in 3D design workflows.

title: Modular Library (Ver. 2025.0)
content: **Table of Contents** Modular Library (2025.0) Structure of The Modular Library Group and Category Line Style Block Auto Modular Labeling Modular Configurator Save Style Save Block Modular Library Options ### ### ## Modular Library ### Objective Quickly and easily create different variations using previously saved garment blocks within Marvelous Designer. This section contains all of your blocks for mixing and matching different styles. Here you can also create and save: Groups, Categories, Styles, and Blocks. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Window ▶ Modular Library Side Panel Title Bar ▶ Right-click Dropdown Menu ▶ Modular Library ※Note: The buttons on the top right are: * **Add** (to add in a new Group or Category) * **List** (To switch between a list and icons) * **Refresh** (update to view any changes) #### ![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881) #### Structure of the Libraries By default, the Modular Library is organized by**Group, Category** and**Style.** This is where all of your blocks will be to mix and match different styles and blocks, here you can also create and save groups, categories, styles and blocks. **![Divider_Dash.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143614745)** **Group and Category** Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. **![Modular Library.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143616409)** Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. 1. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button to add your folder to a Group. 2. Doble-click the Group folder to navigate into the Category. 3. in Category stage, click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button and enter the name to add a new category. _**✨Tip:**_ You can copy the path or delete by right-clicking on a Group or Category folder. ### **![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881)** ## Group and Category ### Objective Both of these sections are Folder based; meaning you can bring in folders from anywhere you have access and also create folders anywhere you have access too. ### Operation ### Adding a New Group or Category 1. Click the Add (plus) button on the top Right, and click Add Group. Select the folder you want to add. → The selected folder will be added as a group. 2. Double-click the added group folder, and click the Add (plus) button on the top of the category tab and click Add Category. → The Add Category window appears. 3. Enter the category name and click the OK button. → The category is added to the selected group. ### Editing Group or Category 1. Select the folder you want to edit and Right click to see your options 1. Copy the Path → Path to the explorer folder is copied. 2. Delete → The folder is deleted. ### ## Line _This is an optional sub-category or "stage" between Category and Style._ Add a Line tier between Category and Style to create a more precise and detailed library structure. 1. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button in the Style stage and click **Group Style by Line** option. 2. In Add Line window, set the name and thumbnail and click **OK** button. → It becomes the upper level above Style in the hierarchy. This allows multiple styles to be grouped under a Line. 3. Click ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) **Add** button on the right side of the Line to add another Line. _**✨Tip:**_ When clicking **Add Line with Same Style** option, all Styles and Blocks within the selected Line are duplicated and added as a new Line. This can be useful when you want to reuse the same structure but make slight changes to some Styles or Blocks. 4. Right-click on the Line thumbnail to delete the selected Line or, change its thumbnail and name. #### ## ** **Style The style is the what all your blocks will be linked to. It is best to think of the different styles as a type of fit so that all your blocks can easily fit together when mixing and matching different blocks. #### ※ Note: The name of the group and category that this style is saved in, is at the top left. ![Modular Library1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438081751833) ### Adding Style 1. After making Category, you can create Style. Double-click the category folder in which you want to add a style, and click the Add button on the top of the style tab. → Style Section window appears. → If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. 2. If you want to register thumbnail manually, click the camera icon and open the image file. 3. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. → Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. ### Editing Style 1. 1. Select the Style you want to edit and Right Click → The Style Selection pop up will come up again and allow you to change the Thumbnail, and Style Name. 2. Delete → If there are blocks within this style a Warning will pop up that the blocks included will be erased and to ask if you would still like to proceed. ![a6e62ca1-0e8a-4a11-811f-2edb3f31548a](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036249881) ## Block These are the different pattern pieces that make up one full style. You can add in multiple patterns for one block, they will be what you will use to mix and create different variations of a style. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438050383641) #### Adding a Block Section ※Note: For automatic block creation, please refer to the "Auto Block Creation" section below. 1. Click the thumbnail of the style that you want to add block, then click the Add (plus) icon and click Add Block Type on the top right. → Create Add Block Type window appears. ※ Note: Style needs to be added in order to add Block. 2. After setting the information below, click the OK button. Type | Set the block type ---|--- Tag | Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten. → the block type is added to the selected style. ### Adding a Pattern to a Block Section 1. 1. Within the added Block Section select the Add (plus) icon. → A Modular Creator pop up window will appear. 2. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. → To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key → Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board 3. The Block Section window will pop up → The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window → If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select the camera icon to create New Thumbnail 4. The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library ### Additional Options 1. Right-Click the block thumbnail you want to edit 2. Select the appropriate menu options as needed. Delete Selected Block | Deletes the selected Block. ---|--- Share Selected Block | Share the selected block with other styles. Any changes made to the block will apply to all shared instances. Change Thumbnail | Change the thumbnail. Replace with New Block | Replace the existing block with a new one. ### Auto Modular Labeling Auto Modular Labeling is based on the results learned from numerous pattern data and analyzes which part of the pattern it is based on only the shape of the pattern. 1. Click ![AI Active.svg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438036889369) **Auto Modular Labeling** button at the top right of the Style stage. → The automatically recognized blocks will be highlighted in colors corresponding to each block type. ![Modular Library3.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358143655449) 2. Check all that all patterns in the 2D window are properly assigned to the correct block types using the Modular Creator. 2-1. If any patterns are not recognized correctly, you can manually adjust or relabel them by clicking **![edit.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157792665)Edit Block** button in the Modular Creator. 2-2. In the 2D window, select the patterns that match the block type you chose and then press the Enter key. _* You can select multiple patterns by holding the Shift key. _ 2-3. In Add Block File window, set the name and thumbnail and click**OK** button. _* The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window._ 3. Click ![Button-1.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157793945) **Save Block** button to set thumbnail image and file name, then click **OK** button. → The Check mark will then be activated to signal that this block is ready. 4. Click**Add** button. 5. After checking whether the block pattern is sewn well with other block patterns, click **OK** button. _* If you need to reset the sewing line, click the Cancel button to correct the sewing line and try again._ ※Note: If you are adding a new block based on an existing block file, you can add it directly without going through the Modular Creator by clicking ![add.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47358157785753) Add button within each Block section, such as Front Body or Sleeves. ### ### ## Modular Configurator This is specifically for saving out style or blocks. This method brings you directly to the Modular Creator which makes saving out styles or blocks a little quicker. #### ### Save Style: 1. Select the Group & Category to save this style under → Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top 2. Select the Add button to add a new Style 3. The Style Section Window will appear → If there is a garment in the 3D window, the thumbnail for that garment is automatically registered. 4. If you want to register thumbnail manually, select Create New Thumbnail and open the image file. 5. Enter the name of the style and press OK button. → Style will be added with the thumbnail and the name. #### ### Save Block: 1. Select the Group & Category to save this style under → Can also create a new Group or Category using the add button at the top 2. Select the Style to save the blocks under → Can also create a new style using the add button at the top 3. Add in the Block Type using the Add button at the top ※Note: Can also use the Auto Block Creation tool this will automatically add in all the blocks and assign all patterns to the coinciding blocks 4. Create New Block Type window appears. → After setting the information below, click the OK button. **Type** | Set the block type ※Note:→ the block type is added to the selected style. ---|--- **Tag** | Enter the block tag. If you need to add 2 or more of the same type, categorize them through tags. When the types and tags are added in the same status, the existing block type will be overwritten 5. The Patterns for that block will then be selectable within the 2D window. → To select multiple pattern hold down the shift key → Once all the pattern are selected hit Enter on your key board 6. The Block Section window will pop up. → The Block thumbnail will automatically be added based on 3D window → If you want to register a thumbnail manually you can select create New Thumbnail. 7. The Thumbnail and name will automatically be added to the Block Section in the Modular Library. ## ## Modular Library Options Here is where you can configure Modular setting / options. 1. Click Main Menu ▶ Settings ▶ Preferences ▶ Other in the top menu. Configure Modular Options as needed. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Default Folder** | Set the default location that the Modular Library saves the Style presets to. **Modular Access** | **Protect Modular Library to Restrict Editing** | Restrict all editing in the Modular Library to protect its original configuration. **Prevent Blocks Mix and Match across Different Styles** | To protect the users from apply different block fits together, turn on the option Prevent Mix and Match. When Prevent Mix and Match is active a Warning pop up will appear when a block from one style is being applied to a separate style. **Notch Sewing** | To save out a specific sewing relationship activate the Notching Sewing option. The Modular Sewing tags will then follow the notch placements for sewing relationships.
content_description: The purpose of this web page is to provide a comprehensive guide for users to efficiently navigate and utilize the Modular Library in Marvelous Designer for creating and managing garment block variations, styles, and configurations.

title: ZIPPER: Edit Zipper
content: ## Objective Edits the length of the zipper. ## Location Main Menu ▶ Materials ▶ Zipper ▶ **Edit Zipper** 3D Toolbar ▶ **![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51994437007257) Edit Zipper** ## ## Operation 1. Click the tool or menu in Location. 2. Click the end point of the zipper and drag in direction to be edited, 3. Then release the mouse to confirm the position. 4. D the end point of the opposite zipper and drag it the same way. → A **blue dot** appears when the length matches the one modified on the opposite side. 5. Then release the mouse to confirm the position. 6. Both lengths of the zipper are modified.

title: Pleats
content: ## **Objective** Create the desired shape of pleats to Patterns. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ 2D Pattern ▶ Pleats ▶ **Pleats** 2D Toolbar ▶ **![Pleats.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/51784511607961)Pleats** ## **Operation** 1. Select the tool/menu indicated in Location. 2. Click to create a start point and an endpoint of a reference line of the pleats along Pattern Outlines. → A Pattern is divided into two. 3. Click on the side where the pleats will be added. → The Pleats window appears. 4. Configure the options and select OK. **Pleats Type** | Select the type of the pleats (Knife, Box, or Accordion). ---|--- **Specification** | Number of Pleats | Decide the number of pleats. Depth | Assign the depth of the pleats (the depth of folded pleats). Interval | Set the interval between pleats when there are two or more pleats. Reverse Direction | Reverse the direction where the pleats will be added. **Option** | Assign fold angles to the fold lines. Greater the difference between the angle of Outside Fold and Inside Fold, sharper the folds are. → The pleats are created on the Pattern. → If there is an Internal Line in the Pattern, it is also moved and rotated along with the Pattern. **※ Note:** * If the segment where pleats are to be created is sewn to another Pattern, the pleats will be automatically sewn in place based on the pleat type selected. If the segment is not sewn, use the **Pleats Sewing** tool to sew the pleats to the other Pattern. * Pleats are dependent on segment point locations. When a pleat is started between two segment points, it will not go further than the next segment point and will result in an error/ red color to indicate this.
content_description: This web page provides a step-by-step guide for creating and customizing pleats in 2D patterns using the appropriate tools and settings.

title: MetaHuman DNA Importer
content: ## **Objective** [**MetaHuman**](https://www.metahuman.com/en-US) is a next-generation digital human creation technology introduced by Epic Games, offering ultra-realistic character modeling and rigging that are almost indistinguishable from reality. Based on high-resolution 3D scans of real people, it enables precise expression of facial features, skin textures, hair, and body proportions, and works seamlessly with **Unreal Engine** for use in films, games, virtual fittings, and more. Now, **Marvelous Designer** allows direct import of **MetaHuman DNA data** , enabling garment creation that reflects realistic facial structures and body proportions with exceptional accuracy. ※ Note: DNA is the file format (*.dna) used for MetaHuman data. ## **Location** Main Menu ▶ File ▶ Import/Import(Add) ▶ DNA ## **Operation** 1. Prepare the Body and Head files (*.dna) extracted from the MetaHuman Editor (Unreal Engine). 2. Go to **File** ▶ **Import/Import (Add)** ▶**DNA** to open the **MetaHuman DNA Importer** dialog. 3. Load both the Body and Head DNA files. 4. Set the additional import options 5. A seamless MetaHuman combining the Head and Body will be loaded as an Avatar type. ## **Options** Options | Description ---|--- **File** | **Body** | Load the Body file of the MetaHuman. **Head** | Load the Head file of the MetaHuman. **Basic** | **Unit** | Select the desired unit and enter the scale as a numerical value. **Options** | **Auto Add Arrangement Points** | For humanoid avatars only, arrangement points are automatically generated in the import process. **Auto Create Fitting Suit** | For humanoid avatars only, a Fitting Suit is automatically created in the import process. **Axis Conversion** | Modifying Object's Axis direction. ※ Note: * Enable **Avatar Display** ▶**Show Avatar Joint** to control the pose in your desired form. * Create animations by setting keyframes on the joints. * Applying motion files(*.mtn) is not supported.
content_description: Discover how to seamlessly import MetaHuman DNA data into Marvelous Designer for ultra-realistic garment creation that perfectly matches the intricate details of digital human avatars.

title: Simulation
content: ### ### Objective Use this function to apply gravity and drape the 3D Garments in the 3D Garment window. Pressing the Simulate button causes all 3D Garments to fall toward the floor and drape onto Avatars and similar objects with collision that are in the way. ### Location Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Simulate** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Simulate** ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ **Simulate** 3D Toolbar ▶ **Simulate** →3D Garments in the 3D window drapes on Avatars. →When the Simulation is activated, the tool automatically switches to the **Select/Move** tool (ver5.1.0.) **※Note:** * Simulation presets are added to the 3D toolbar (ver. 4.2.0). Long press the Simulate tool icon to access the additional options. Name | Description ---|--- **Normal (Default)** | Select Simulate(Normal) when working on a 3D Garment. \- When the simulation preset is set to Simulate(Normal), You can work on the 3D Garment efficiently with the fastest simulation speed setting. **Animation (Stable)** | Garment simulation is more defined with higher simulation quality settings, the simulation speed will likely decrease. \- Use this preset when recording animation caches. **Fitting** **(Accurate Fabric)** | Garment simulation is more defined and fabric stretch is expressed more realistically, this is the slowest but most accurate to real world simulation setting. **Processor** | **CPU** | CPU based simulation. **GPU** | GPU based simulation. Depending on the computer specification, the simulation speed can increase. ※ Note: GPU simulation feature is greatly improved in (ver. 2024.2) with same collision handing accuracy as CPU simulation. The results from CPU and GPU based simulations are matched, with minimal differences. **※ Note:** * Users can select CPU/GPU from simulation toolbar with different simulation presets. (ver. 2024.2) * Animation (Stable) is added into Simulation Toolbar. Users may opt to run simulations prior to recording an animation. (ver. 2024.2) * **GPU acceleration for Trim Simulation and Soft Body Simulation are limited in the current version.** (ver. 2024.2) * Adjustments to 2D Patterns' points and segments are reflected in the 3D window in real-time (ver. 4.2.0). The real-time Simulation (Interactive Editing) is unavailable from Marvelous Designer ver. 4.2.0's last patch. * Even during heavy computational load, the simulation can be stopped instantly. (ver. 2025.2)
content_description: Explore how to simulate and drape 3D garments onto avatars in the 3D Garment window using various preset options for enhanced realism and efficiency.

title: Pins
content: ### Objective Create, Delete, and other functions relating to Pin tool. * Create Pin * Delete Pin * Duplicate Pins To Symmetric Pattern * Attach / Detach Pins from Avatar ## Create Pin ### Objective Affix specific portions of the Garment and utilize Pin similar to the Freeze function. It is also convenient when turning/flipping over collars, lapels, or cuffs. ### Location #### Pin Tool Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click for more than 2 seconds) ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) #### Select/Move Tool Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Select/Move 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ### Operation #### Pin Tool 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) 3D Toolbar ▶ (Click more than 2 seconds) ▶ Pin (Box) / Pin (Lasso) → The Garment mesh is now displayed in red in both the 3D and 2D windows. 2. Click on a vertex (a point of the mesh). → A Pin is created on the selected point. 3. Or click on a desired area on the Garment ▶ Click and drag to select the area. → Pins are created on the vertex of the selected area. → Pins can also be created on 2D Patterns. 4. Click and drag, or use the Gizmo to move the pinned mesh as desired in the 3D window. ※ Note: Click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Shift + Ctrl on the keyboard to create additional pinned areas. Adversely, click and drag on the 2D Pattern while pressing Ctrl on the keyboard to remove Pins from existing pinned areas. #### Select/Move Tool 1. Click on the Select/Move tool in the 3D window. 2. Click while pressing W on the keyboard to create a Pin on a specific point. → A Pin is created on the selected point. 3. If the input language is set to Korean, a Pin cannot be created when pressing W on the keyboard. Make sure to change the input language to English. ※ Note: * #### Create Pin on Segment Double-click on a Pattern outline in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a segment. When creating Pins on the Pattern in the 2D window, Pins are generated on adjacent segment vertices when the angle difference is less than 20˚. * #### Create Pin on Pattern Double-click on a Pattern in either the 3D or 2D window to create Pins on a Pattern. * #### Create Pin on Internal Line (ver4.0.0) Use the same procedure as above to create Pins on specific Internal Lines and Shapes. * #### Select All Pins on the Same Pattern (ver 2025.2) Double-clicking a created Pin selected all Pins placed on the same pattern at once. ## Delete Pin ### Objective Delete unnecessary pins. ### Location Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins ### Operation 1. Follow the indicated guideline below: Main Menu ▶ Edit ▶ Context Menu ▶ 3D Garment ▶ Delete All Pins / Delete All Pins on Selected Patterns Pin Right-Click Pop-Up Menu ▶ Delete Selected Pin / Delete All Pins → The selected pin is now being deleted. ※ Note: Selecting a created pin while holding W key on keyboard also deletes the pin. ## Duplicate Pins To Symmetric Pattern (ver. 2024.2) ### Objective Added the ability to reflect pins onto the symmetric pattern, including all pin details such as pin position. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) ### Operation 1. Create pins by following guideline in the**Location** above. 2. In 3D window, right-click on the Pin/Pins in the scene. 3. Click the option "Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern" 4. Duplicate Pin/Pins are created on the other side of the Symmetric pattern with all the pin details including the position of the Pin/Pins 5. When Simulating, both sides will be Symmetrical with Pins. ※ Note: * If a pattern with no symmetry is selected, and trying to apply this ‘Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern’ option. A pop-up box will appear with error message: “Some Pattern/Patterns has no symmetry applied. Duplicate to Symmetric Pattern can only be applied to pattern with Symmetry“ * If a set of pins on multiple patterns is added and some of them have Symmetry and the others don't. The function will apply pins only on the respective symmetric pattern with the above pop-up message box. ## Attach / Detach Pins from Avatar ### Objective Affix specific parts of the Garments to the Avatar. This function is commonly used for Simulation or recording animation for avoiding the Garment sliding off from the Avatar. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) ### Operation #### Attach Pin to Avatar 1. Create a pin to attach to an Avatar. 2. Follow the indicated guideline below: 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move or Select Mesh (Box) or Pin (Box) 3. Right-click on the created pin ▶ select Attach Pin to Avatar/Attach All Pins to Avatar. → The selected pin is now being attached to the nearest part of the Avatar. ※ Note: Pins attached to the Avatar are unable to be selected or moved. #### Detach Pin from Avatar 1. Right-click on the pin attached to the avatar ▶ select Detach from Avatar/Detach All Pins from Avatar. → The attached pin is now being detached from the Avatar.
content_description: This web page serves as a comprehensive guide for utilizing the Pin tool, detailing functions such as creating, deleting, and managing pins on garments for enhanced design and simulation.

For instance, draping and freezing inner Garments first, then draping outerwear simultaneously, solves the occasional instabilities. ### Location 3D Toolbar ▶ Select/Move ▶ 3D Garment Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Freeze / Unfreeze 2D Toolbar ▶ Transform Pattern ▶ 2D Pattern Right-Click Pop-up Menu ▶ Freeze / Unfreeze ### Operation 1. title: Print on Fabric
content: **List of Contents** Add Print Print Properties Copy Print Print various patterns on Fabric. ### **Add Print** 1. Click **Add Print** to the right of the Fabric in Fabric tab of the Object Browser. 2. Select the desired image. → A print item is added under the fabric item. ### **Print Properties** 1. title: Denim Wet Wash Effect
content: **New in 2025.1** Apply Wash Parameters **** Express Denim wet wash effects without using external software and avoid many back-and-forth steps. #### **Apply** 1. Change the Material Type to the**Denim** → It is applied as unwashed by default. 2. Apply the denim texture as the Base Color Map. 3. Set the Denim **Wet Process** type. → The wash effects are applied on the Fabric's Base Color Map. 4. Assign the **Wash Map** and adjust the **Wash Parameters** to achieve the desired result. #### **Wash Parameters** Adjust the wash parameters to express realistic wet wash effects. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Wet Process** | **Wash Map** | Apply a texture map to achieve the wash effect. **Transformation** | Scale, rotate or move the Wash Effect **Softerners/Enzyme Concentration/** **FadingIntensity/** **Concentration/Map Intensity** | Set the wash effect intensity on the Base Color Map. **Blend** | Plenty of Blending options are provided, which decide how the wash effect blends with the base Fabric. _* Overlay is recommended for the majority of Denim washes._ **Absorbency** | Adjust how deeply these effects need to be absorbed/spread in the Base Fabric. * Keep the Absorbency minimal(0~20) with the seamless wash effect map to avoid repeat issue **Cycle Duration** | Sets the Cycle Duration/Washing Time. Longer duration removes more dye/color from the yarn (Base Color Map). **Seam Abrasion** | Enhance the Base Color Map of Puckering applied to the pattern with the respective Fabric.
content_description: Explore the new **Apply Wash Parameters** feature in 2025.1 to effortlessly create realistic denim wet wash effects directly, streamlining your design process without the need for external software.

title: Import and Export Preset
content: **New in MD 2025.1** **Add Preset** **Preset Options** **Supported File Formats** When Importing or Exporting 3D files, users can save their configured options as a preset for reuse. These preset files can also be shared, allowing users to distribute organizational standards and policies. #### #### Add Preset 1. Go to **File > Import/Export** to import 3D file. 2. Configure the desired options in the Import dialog. 3. Click the **Preset > ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48920118220057)Add **button at the top of the dialog. 4. In the **Create Configuration** dialog, set the **Preset Path** and **Name**. 5. Click Save button to store the preset. The saved preset will then be selected in the Preset dropdown. * The saved preset can be selected during future imports to consistently apply the configured settings * Default Path: C:\Users\Public\Documents\MarvelousDesigner\Configuration\Preset\Import #### #### Preset Options **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Add** | Add a new preset. **Remove** | Delete the currently selected preset. **Open Folder** | Open the folder where the currently selected preset is saved. #### #### Supported File Formats Only 3D file formats are supported * OBJ, FBX, Alembic, USD * Maya Cache (MC, MCX), Point Cache 2, MDD Cache (Standard, Maya/3ds Max), OBJ Sequence **📝 Note:** * Each 3D file type uses its own dedicated JSON file and cannot be used with other types. * e.g., an Export FBX preset cannot be used for Export OBJ * Import and Export used separate dedicated JSON files. * e.g., an Import FBX preset cannot be used for Export FBX

Enter your pattern measurement values. _**✨Tip:** _ ▪️You can return each measurement to its original value individually by clicking ![reset.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075972761) **Reset** button. ▪️Certain Measurements include ![Total.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075974169)**Total** option to input the full front and back circumference. ▪️Certain measurements include dropdown options, as they are commonly taken from different areas of the pattern. **\- Total Length:** High Point Shoulder, Or Center Front/ Back **\- Across Front/ Back:** 4", 5" or 6" from High Point shoulder **\- Across Waist:** 4", 5" or 6" from Armhole **\- Across Bust/ Chest:** Armhole to Armhole or 1" from Armhole **\- Bicep Width:** Armhole to Armhole or 1" from Armhole ▪️For the Front and Back Body, you can choose between **Symmetry** and **Half Symmetry**. ▪️You can view all inactive measurements in each section by clicking ![list.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950075975321) **Show All Measurements** icon. #### **AI Pattern Drafter (Beta)** Using a Sketch Marvelous Designer will Automatically generate measurements to create a drafted pattern for you. 1. Click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/49886528028441) **AI Pattern Drafter (Beta)** button on the top right of the Pattern Drafter. ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276717721) 2. Generate a background image to be composited by entering prompts or upload it directly. **Option** | **Description** ---|--- **Text Prompt** | Select the garment type and write in your sketch idea. Make sure to add in as many descriptive words as possible. if you want to emphasize something place it in brackets. ※ Supporting Type: **T-Shirts, Pants, and Skirts.** (There will be more coming.) **✨ Writing Tips:** Listing the desired words rather than long descriptive sentences can generate more effective results. ![Comment.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950284431001)**Keyword Suggestions** | Suggested keywords will appear as you type to help you complete your prompt. ![icon_pin_off.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276732057)**Maintain Prompt** | Even if the same prompts are used, the AI Face image is created anew each time. Thus, clicking the Maintain Prompt button may update the prompts while preserving the existing results as much as possible. The results may differ from the existing ones depending on the addition or change of the prompts. ![icon_random_dice.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276734489) **Random** | Sample prompts are provided randomly ![Editor Edit.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276735257) **Clear** | Clear anything that was written to restart. **Image** | Click the **Upload** button to load a face image that fits the following guidelines: A schematic image of the garment with black lines on a white background is highly recommended to ensure the highest quality of the AI Pattern. Ensure the image shows the garment only. 3. Click ![](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/48950276738969) button and an image will be generated for you to choose from. This process can be replicated until you get the desired outcome. Your image history can be found on the right side of the window.

Find the Tile menu in the Property Editor and adjust the settings below as needed: Option | Description ---|--- Revert to Original | Reset the graphic to its original configuration before this function was used. X-Axis | Repeat the graphic along the x-axis of the pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. Y-Axis | Repeat the graphic along the y-axis of the pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. Pattern | Repeat the graphic across the entire pattern, while maintaining its dimensions. → The selected graphic will be tiled according to the menu selection. Via the Right-Click Pop-Up Menu 1. Navigate to Tile and select from the available options (same as Property Editor). → The selected graphic will be tiled according to the menu selection. ※Note: When a graphic is repeated using this function, its Graphic Transformation ▶ Original Width and Original Height values will change.

title: [Tips&Tricks] Discover Better Workflow with Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine
content: Through our collaborative efforts, we’re excited to introduce two new features for our community: the LiveSync plugin and USD export simulation data. In this article, we’ll explore how these powerful tools can elevate your workflow. Both the**LiveSync plugin** and **USD Export for Simulation Data** are tailored for users who frequently toggle between Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, but each serves a different purpose. * **LiveSync Plugin** : The feature is primarily aimed at simplifying the tedious import and export process. mesh, materials, skeletal animations, and geometry caches can all be imported and exported with just one click. * **USD Export Simulation Data** : Specifically designed to work with Unreal Engine 5.4's updated **Chaos Cloth** feature, this tool enables real-time simulation effects, translating complex clothing physics from Marvelous Designer directly into Unreal Engine. Let’s dive into how these tools enhance the design and animation workflow by walking through a case study featuring a fairy character animation sequence. ![Cenimetics_cc03_Still001.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438057410201) ## **Designing the Fairy Garment in Marvelous Designer** Before we jump into Unreal Engine, let's explore how we crafted the fairy's outfit in Marvelous Designer. ** ** **1\. Starting with a Simple T-Shirt Base** Marvelous Designer offers multiple ways to begin garment creation. For this project, we started by dragging a T-shirt pattern into the 2D window as a base. With the **Style Line tool,** we could quickly split and modify the T-shirt into a completely different style by adjusting the pattern directly in the 3D window, with real-time updates reflected in the 2D pattern. ![StyleLine_merged.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437978960409)**2\. Layering and Fabric Simulation** Marvelous Designer excels in simulating multi-layered garments. For the fairy outfit, we duplicated the underskirt pattern and added lace detail using internal lines. Each layer contributes to the garment’s dynamic, three-dimensional look. To simulate different fabric properties, we added a Muslin fabric preset from Marvelous Designer’s library of 77 fabric types, which changes the folds and flow of the skirt during simulation. ![08.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438009386649) **3\. Creating Petal Patterns and Pleating Effects** Using the Polygon Tool, we traced petal shapes for the skirt from a photo, then applied accordion pleat effect with the Internal Polygon Tool and Pleat Tool. The result was an elegant, multi-layered skirt with beautiful texture and movement. Thanks to Marvelous Designer's new PBR Texture Generator, we were also able to auto-generate texture maps (normal, opacity, metalness, displacement) with a single click, further enhancing the realism.![flower_paddle.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438009738777) ![06.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438009893657) **4\. Adding Ruffles and Topstitching**** **For the finishing touch, we created ruffles by sewing longer pattern edges onto shorter ones. And using the**Topstitch Tool** , we added stitching details that elevated the garment’s realism. ![TopStitch.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438058599321) After completing the garment design and the initial simulation in Marvelous Designer, we move on to caching the animation. ## **Animation Caching** First, using the **Pin Tool** , we secure certain parts of the garment to the character model by double-clicking the edge lines of the pattern pieces, quickly pinning the entire line. The **Tack Tool** is another way we can constrain the fabric to the model, while also allowing for length adjustments that control the distance between the fabric and the model. To cache the animation, we change the simulation preset to **Animation** , reduce the gravity value and increase air damping to simulate a floating, fairy-like effect. When all settings are in place, we click **Record** to start recording the animation cache. This cache will store all the necessary animation data, which can later be exported to Unreal Engine with full fidelity, preserving all simulation effects.** ** ## ![MD_Sim.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438058798361)**Calla Lily Creation** The vegetation in the scene is also modeled and simulated using Marvelous Designer. During the animation recording process, we can adjust the position and angle of the wind in real-time to create these natural dynamic effects. Marvelous Designer’s keyframe editing tool allows us to create perfect looping animations without frame skips—ideal for in-game sequences. Similar to video editing tools, we can cut layers and move layers horizontally. Copy the first frame and paste it at the end of the animation. The last frame of the animation blends into the first frame, creating a perfect cycle animation.** ** ![CalaLily.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438058959257) Once the animation was complete, both the fairy's garment and the calla lily were imported into Unreal Engine using the LiveSync Plugin, which maintains the accuracy of materials, animations, and textures during the transfer. ## **Transfer to Unreal Engine with LiveSync** Now that the fairy’s garment is complete, it’s time to bring the animation into Unreal Engine using the **LiveSync plugin**. After Install and Activate LiveSync, ensure that Marvelous Designer is running, then open the **LiveSync Editor** in Unreal Engine, and click the “Update” button.** ** ![LiveSync.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437980377625) The scene in Marvelous Designer is imported into the LiveSync Editor. In the editor, we can see that the shader balls have been automatically created based on the fabrics assigned in Marvelous Designer. We can also activate Unified Material; by clicking update again, the plugin will generate unified materials based on UV coordinates.![calalily_02.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438026338969)The capabilities of the **LiveSync plugin** aren’t limited to importing. MetaHuman characters, or any skeletal meshes, can be exported to and from Unreal Engine. Making it easier to create and simulate clothing for your characters. With all assets successfully imported, we used Unreal Engine’s **Sequencer** to animate and render the final scene. The fairy’s clothing, wings, and environment elements like calla lilies were all modeled and simulated in Marvelous Designer before being synchronized with Unreal Engine via the **LiveSync plugin**. ![light.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438011161625) ## **Leveraging Chaos Cloth with USD Export** **![gameplay_01.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437994671641)**The LiveSync plugin is suitable for rendering animations, creating videos, and cinematics using Unreal Engine. It can also be used to import environmental assets from Marvelous Designer (such as the calla lilies in this scene). But for users seeking real-time fabric simulation, Marvelous Designer’s**USD Export Simulation Data** is an invaluable asset, especially when paired with Unreal Engine’s **Chaos Cloth**. Let’s break down the process:** ** ![S01.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438060052249) **Optimizing for Chaos Cloth** : The fairy’s garment, with its complex layering, needed to be optimized before importing into Unreal Engine. By splitting the dress into three parts—skinned mesh, simulation mesh, and render mesh. ![05.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438043457817)**Auto-Retopology** and **Rigging** : The garment that does not need to participate in the simulation is skinned to the character’s body. The close-fitting garment does not need to participate in the simulation. Using Marvelous Designer’s **EveryWear Toolkit** , we performed automatic retopology and rigging. EveryWear is an automatic optimization toolkit for virtual clothing in games. Marvelous Designer's Quad Optimize option can achieve auto retopology. And with the EveryWear tool, we can reduce the polygon count. Rigging feature is also a part of EveryWear tool set. We can first specify the maximum number of influencing joints. Unreal Engine supports a maximum of 8 joints, so we set it to 8. Click 'Apply,' and the weights of the body mesh will automatically be copied to the garment. The skin weight can be painted and smooth using the brush tools. And we can use Hammer Tool and Repair brushes from the sculpting toolset to fix any intersections. ![Retpop.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438027448729)![Rigging.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438032351769) The primary challenge with this fairy's dress is that the petal skirt has too many layers, making it heavy and complex. The approach we used to optimize the skirt was to represent the multiple layers through textures instead of geometry. First, we split the skirt into two parts and unfolded it. Then, we created a simplified proxy model and used an orthographic view to render different AOV channels as texture maps. This significantly simplified the geometry, while the textures gave the illusion of layered complexity. ![04.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438060833689)![04 copy.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437995843737) (The left image shows the skirt unfolded in Marvelous Designer, and the right image illustrates how these layers are represented using textures.) ## **Optimizing Polygon Count** To further optimize the model, we need to reduce the polygon count. One way to do this is by increasing the particle distance in Marvelous Designer. When simulating fabric in 3D, random triangles tend to create more natural-looking folds. Using triangular meshes instead of quads works well with Chaos Cloth in Unreal Engine, so there’s no need to retopologize or convert to quads. Simply increasing the particle distance value will reduce the number of faces. Another important factor is increasing the collision thickness, which creates more separation between fabric layers. In this case, the collision thickness was increased from the default 2.5 mm to 5 mm for better results in Chaos Cloth.** ** ## ![CollisionThickness_03.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438032993177)**Exporting the USD File ** Once the model is optimized, we can export the USD file. Uncheck the option to export all avatars, select multiple objects in the export settings, and enable the "thick" option and unified UV coordinates. Crucially, ensure that the **Include garment simulation data** option is enabled. This will preserve all the physical properties assigned in Marvelous Designer, such as shrinkage and collision settings, so they can be read by Unreal Engine’s Chaos Cloth. ![SimulationProp \(1\).png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438033211929) ## **ClothAsset Setup in Unreal Engine** Back in Unreal Engine, we need to create a **ClothAsset**. Import the USD file exported from Marvelous Designer and select the skeletal mesh, which was also imported using the Marvelous Designer LiveSync plugin. This process skins the clothing to the character. In the preview scene, make sure to select the same skeletal mesh again.** ** ## **Painting Weights for Maximum Distance** Next, we’ll paint weights for the maximum distance property. It controls which parts of the fabric will participate in the simulation. Areas painted with 0 value represent regions that will not be simulated and are instead skinned directly to the character’s body. Use a smooth brush to create a gradient effect for the weights. You can paint weights in either the 2D or 3D views. If working in 2D, the layout and arrangement of the patterns are identical to what we see in the 2D window of Marvelous Designer. To make it easy for weight painting, make sure to pay attention to the layout of the patterns before exporting the USD file. The pattern pieces should not be too close together or have any overlapping. After painting the weights, click 'Accept' to preview the simulation results.** ** ![03.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438013248537) The weight values we painted can be adjusted using the **SimulationMaxDistanceConfig** node, which controls the highest and lowest weight values. Lowering the maximum value can further optimize the simulation. ## ## **Fabric Physical Properties ** The next three nodes are used to define the physical properties of the fabric. Normally, adjusting fabric properties is the most complex part of cloth simulation, but since we exported the physical properties from Marvelous Designer, this step becomes much simpler. By enabling the arrow icon on each parameter, we can directly use the fabric properties imported from Marvelous Designer.** ** ![SimData.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47437996767769) Additionally, a clothing icon next to the nodes allows us to use the weight map generated in Marvelous Designer. Different fabric presets were applied to different patterns in Marvelous Designer, and the weight map is automatically exported with the USD file. ![SimData02.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438029196185) To enable the clothing to collide with the character’s body, we need to create a physics asset. This asset should be added to the **SetPhysicsAsset** node in Unreal Engine. ## ![PhysicsAssets.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438062365977)**Other Key Nodes for Cloth Simulation** * **SimulationCollisionConfig** : Controls fabric thickness and friction. Enabling the arrow icon will use values imported from Marvelous Designer. * **Self Collision** : Disabled by default for optimization. Enabling it will allow basic self-collision using spheres. Or use the more precise but more costly collisions through the **SimulationSelfCollisionConfig node.** * **SimulationSolverConfig:** This node manages global settings for the solver. Increasing the number of iterations strengthens the stiffness of constraints, but increases CPU load. Adjust the **Substep** value to improve collision accuracy at the cost of higher CPU load. Both settings must be optimized for performance and accuracy. You can also add aerodynamic effects to the simulation. By introducing wind fields, the clothing will move naturally during idle animations, making the character appear more lifelike. ## ## **Level of Detail (LOD) Settings** The final part of the preset involves configuring **LOD (Level of Detail)** settings. Different LODs will activate based on the camera’s distance from the character. The physical properties we configured earlier are connected to the top collection. A **Remesh** node is added to the middle LOD collection to reduce mesh density. The bottom collection, connected directly from the skinning node, doesn’t include dynamic simulation. If we want fabric simulation to be active all the time during gameplay, this collection can be removed.** ** ![02.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438034423193) ## ## **Merging the Simulation and Render Meshes** If a proxy model was used for simulation, we need to remove it as the render mesh using a**Delete Elements** node. Then, import a detailed render mesh, either as a static mesh or through a USD import node. Then use the **Merge Cloth Collection** node to combine the simulation mesh with the new render mesh.** ** ![RenderMesh.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438062736025) ## ** Final Setup in the Character Blueprint** In the character’s blueprint, add a**Chaos Cloth Component** and parent it to the character. Select the cloth asset we just created and adjust the position and rotation parameters if necessary. Compile and save the blueprint.** ** ![Character.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438048068761) Now, the clothing has real-time fabric simulation properties and will react naturally in the game environment. ![Still.jpg](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438048200601)Whether you’re creating cinematic sequences or in-game assets, the combination of Marvelous Designer’s **LiveSync plugin** and **USD Export Simulation Data** delivers a seamless, efficient workflow. The tools allow for rich, detailed simulations and quick iterations, significantly enhancing productivity. ![01.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438030245913)To explore these tools for yourself, the fairy model and garment are available for free download on our official [CONNECT store](https://connect.clo-set.com/). These files are intended for educational use and cannot be used for commercial purposes.
content_description: Discover how the LiveSync plugin and USD export simulation data can transform your design and animation workflow between Marvelous Designer and Unreal Engine, enhancing your projects with seamless integration and real-time fabric simulation.

title: How to Prevent Marvelous Designer File Corruption
content:
**Objective** This article describes why Marvelous Designer project file .zprj and garment file .zpac are corrupted and how to prevent them.
``` Failed to read the Project file: Unzip error~
``` ![Screenshot 2023-01-27 165004.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438263659289) **Problem Situations** * When launching Marvelous Designer, get an error saying failed to read the project file. * When opening a project file saved on the computer, it says it is unreadable. * When trying to save the file, it says it can't be saved. * Opening the file takes a long time and eventually fails. * * * **Causes and Solutions** **Case 1.** **Disk Full... Actually** ![01 - Disk Full.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438263938329) * If disk space is insufficient during the process of designing and saving garments in Marvelous Designer, file corruption may actually occur. So make sure you have enough free space on your PC's drive. * We recommend that you have at least 20GB of free space to install and run Marvelous Designer. You can make free space by deleting or backing up unnecessary files. * **See also: [Marvelous Designer System Requirements](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358219834649)** **Case 2.** **Mechanical Malfunction and/or Connection Failure** ![02 - Mechanical-Malfunction.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438264140441) * File corruption may occur due to physical failure, disk error, or poor connection. * You can check disk status through the built-in disk management app or disk management utility on Windows and macOS. * In case of physical failure, contact your company's IT support department or the place of purchase. **Case 3.** **No Permission to File Read and Write** ![03 - No Permission.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438236469145) * All computer operating systems, including Windows and macOS, have permission to read/write your files. If you do not have or only have partial permissions to read/write, Marvelous Designer file corruption may occur. The following post explains how to gain read/write permissions for Marvelous Designer files on Windows and macOS. **[Disk access rights required when Marvelous Designer running](https://marvelousdesigner-hc.zendesk.com/hc/en-us/articles/47358175269657)** * If you are a corporate customer, please contact your company's IT/Security department. **Case 4.** **Blocking File Read and Write, or Data Tampering by Security Apps** ![04 - Blocking file RW.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438252037529) * Certain security programs, such as antivirus and Internet communication monitoring tools, may restrict Internet access and file creation of software such as Marvelous Designer. **In their detailed settings, change the Marvelous Designer Internet access and file read/write settings to "Allow".** * In the case of enterprise companies, they often use stronger security solutions than those described above, and in some cases, the files themselves created by Marvelous Designer are tampered with. For corporate users, please contact your IT/Security department. **Case 5.** **Two or More Marvelous Designer Running Simultaneously** ![05 - Two or more CLOs Running.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438249085081) * If you use two or more Marvelous Designer at the same time, there is a possibility that the internal data of the Marvelous Designer project file may be lost or corrupted. * All you know that it's a good way to save file often. And **if you need to save the final result, save it with only one Marvelous Designer running.** **Case 6.** **External Storage Connection Failure** ![06 - External Storage.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438215098393) * File corruption may occur while reading or writing Marvelous Designer files on external storage such as USB stick or portable hard disk. Although these are convenient, in reality, physical detection failures and connection failures are relatively frequent. * When transferring files between an external device and your PC, it often appears that the file-transfer has been complete, but in reality, the all data has not been completely transferred. To check whether the file was completely transferred, simply compare the file size. * **In summary, allow plenty of time when exchanging files with external storage devices.** **Case7** **Network Drive or Cloud Sync Failure** ![07 - Network Drives.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438232214297) * If you use a NAS and various Internet cloud sync services, Marvelous Designer files may be corrupted during file transfer over the network. Additionally, cloud sync services may have problems that removing or damaging files on the local computer during the sync process. * If you use a cloud sync service, set it to sync only specific folders, excluding folders and directories referenced by the Marvelous Designer. **For example, disable syncing your Desktop and Documents folders.** * * * **Read More** **1** For example, the size of the zprj and zpac files, including Marvelous Designer basic t-shirt and basic avatar, is approximately 20MB. If your files are smaller than expected, it means the internal data may be corrupted. If your project file is less than 1MB in size, it cannot be recovered because all clothing data inside the file has been lost. **2** When recording animations of flashy, heavy garments, the project file size will be very large, and this animation recording data may be fragile in some user scenarios. If you are recording a long animation, dividing the entire scene into sections as shown below will help prevent file corruption. ![008_MD.png](https://support.marvelousdesigner.com/hc/article_attachments/47438300166681) * * * **File Recovery** If you would like to recover your file, please send us your problem file as is via **[Contact Us](https://marvelousdesigner.com/support/contact)**.
